I was an early MD adopter buying the original MZ1 portable which was so big it needed to be carried in a satchel style holder. It was front loading and had pretty bad battery life although it took removable portable VCR batteries. It also had optical in and out which was good because I could hook it up to my DAC. That early play had some obvious compression artefacts but overall wasn't too bad. I bought a later more portable walkman style one and they got smaller and with better battery life, then MD-LP came along which doubled the playing time while improving sound. I even got an MD player in my car it was that convenient. I bought a NetMD player thinking it would be great to handle music via computer but it wasn't. The software sucked and the process of copying files over through SoundStage over USB was slow and clumsy. By this point, MP3 players were getting better and I was then offered a brand new iPod 3G 40GB that someone won and didn't want so I sold my MD player and never looked back. MD was always a bit late to the party, although it was way better than DCC at the same time because it wasn't tape based but the advent of CD-R and then MP3 players killed it because they never handled the software side well or interfaced it to a computer until it was far too late and the format was dead. I never bothered with Hi-MD as that arrived after I switched to the iPod. I'm sure it sounded great, but Sony sure has a way of making a good idea work badly. I've got HDDVD and BD and HDDVD was the better format. Quicker menus, better interactivity from the start, better format but here we are and now they bring us 4KBD and I'm not buying.
